Messages.Author: William C Wendel
Messages.Body:
My friends and I have a few questions. Here they are:

1. When in combat, who presses or manuevers first? We think it shouldb
be the attacker, but we don't know.

2. Can you change weapons in the middle of combat? Like can you use a
gun the first round, and then an RPG Launcher the next round if you
press?

3. Can you play Drawing out the Beast on yourself? We don't think so,
but one dumbass keeps asking.

4. Are Jyhad players cooler than Magic players?

5. Re: Talbot's Chainsaw, do you have to untap your card during the

untap phase, or do you basically have to attack every turn unless you
are in torpor? Wouldn't it be best to give it to a low-blooded minion,
and bring him out of torpor with a high-blooded vampire?

Thanks muchachos

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
wwe...@osf1.gmu.edu (William C Wendel) wrote:
>
> My friends and I have a few questions. Here they are:
>
> 1. When in combat, who presses or manuevers first? We think it shouldb
> be the attacker, but we don't know.

Peace William,

The acting minions maneuvers, strikes, and presses first.

> 2. Can you change weapons in the middle of combat? Like can you use a
> gun the first round, and then an RPG Launcher the next round if you
> press?

Yes, you may use several different weapons during the same combat, even
during the same round, for example: you are armed with a .44 Magnum and
a Shotgun and you have Celerity; you can use the .44 to maneuver to range,
then strike with it, then Blur for an additional strike and strike with
the Shotgun (or .44 again).

> 3. Can you play Drawing out the Beast on yourself? We don't think so,
> but one dumbass keeps asking.

No.

> 4. Are Jyhad players cooler than Magic players?

We play a better, more balance game and spend less money doing it.

> 5. Re: Talbot's Chainsaw, do you have to untap your card during the
> untap phase, or do you basically have to attack every turn unless you
> are in torpor? Wouldn't it be best to give it to a low-blooded minion,
> and bring him out of torpor with a high-blooded vampire?

You cannot avoid untapping. You do not have to attack [the (D) action]
with Talbot's Chainsaw every turn, as equipment use is optional. The
three points of damage that the TC does to one of your minions is _not_
optional [it is a cursed chainsaw].

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
wwe...@osf1.gmu.edu (William C Wendel) writes:

>My friends and I have a few questions. Here they are:

>1. When in combat, who presses or manuevers first? We think it shouldb
>be the attacker, but we don't know.

Timing for everything resolves as follows:
Acting player.
Blocking / Targetted PLayer (or Prey then Predator for undirected action).
Other Methuselahs clockwise from acting player.

So, in combat - this is Acting minion before blocking minion.

>2. Can you change weapons in the middle of combat? Like can you use a
>gun the first round, and then an RPG Launcher the next round if you
>press?

Sure. You can even use different weapons for different strikes in the
same round, if you get multiple strikes.

>3. Can you play Drawing out the Beast on yourself? We don't think so,
>but one dumbass keeps asking.

No. "*Opposing* vampire ..." seems clear enough.

>5. Re: Talbot's Chainsaw, do you have to untap your card during the
>untap phase, or do you basically have to attack every turn unless you
>are in torpor? Wouldn't it be best to give it to a low-blooded minion,
>and bring him out of torpor with a high-blooded vampire?

You can never choose not to untap. The untap phase is the only mandatory
phase (Except, thanks DTR, the minion phase if you have a vampire who
must hunt), and the untap phase always begins with untapping *all* of
the cards you control.

Some read the text as indicting a mandatory attack. Some say it is optional.
The rest is conjecture.

The answer to this question is obvious. Magic is a game, Jyhad is an
attitude. Magic players are content with hack and slash - Jyhad players

learned Jyhad after several games, several nights of posting questions,
and many reips to the instruction manual. On the other hand, after

in a devestating Magic deck. For multi- player, there is no contest. I
know of one who does not agree, refuses to try Jyhad - but he plays an
all white deck anyway, and is of no consequence :-)

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3maelh$9...@portal.gmu.edu>,

William C Wendel <wwe...@osf1.gmu.edu> wrote:
>5. Re: Talbot's Chainsaw, do you have to untap your card during the
>untap phase, or do you basically have to attack every turn unless you
>are in torpor? Wouldn't it be best to give it to a low-blooded minion,
>and bring him out of torpor with a high-blooded vampire?

You must always untap every card unless some other card effect
is stopping it. TC has two separate events associated with it. The
first is the untap damage that you must inflict on one of your own
minions, which is mandatory. That damage will have to be assigned if
the minion with TC is ready (face-up and not in torpor). The second
event is the attack it allows against another minion. That attack is
optional, and the minion can use it or not at the player's discretion.

There are several strategies that you can use to make effective
use of TC, and yours is one that can work well.

Messages.Author: Marko Puumalainen
Messages.Body:
"James R. McClure Jr." <jrmc...@ulkyvm.louisville.edu> writes:

>wwe...@osf1.gmu.edu (William C Wendel) wrote:

>> 1. When in combat, who presses or manuevers first? We think it shouldb
>> be the attacker, but we don't know.

>The acting minions maneuvers, strikes, and presses first.

But the acting minion always has a chance to cancel a maneuver. If
one of the combatants wants to maneuver to long range the other has a
chance to cancel that with another maneuver. So it does not matter
which one has to declare maneuver first.

The same goes with presses. If one wants to continue she presses and
then the other has a chance to cancel the press.

Only with strikes it is crucial which one goes first and it's always
the acting minion, and it cannot change the strike afterwards.
